title: Kernel-normalized determinant maps for surjective two-term quasi-isomorphisms
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. A finite projective $R$-module means a direct summand of a finite free module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. For such a module $V$, write $\det_R(V)$ for its determinant module: on each constant-rank locus of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-pc-scheme] it is the top exterior power, with the transition maps induced by exterior powers [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]; equivalently use finite free localizations as in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] and their usual change-of-basis determinant maps. Put $D(P)=\det_R(P^0)\otimes_R\det_R(P^{-1})^\vee$ for a cochain complex $P=[P^{-1}\xrightarrow{d_P}P^0]$ of finite projective modules, zero in other degrees; here $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R(V,R)$. For a degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism $a:P\to Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], let $N^i=\ker(a^i)$ with the induced differential. Then $N^{-1},N^0$ are finite projective and $d_N:N^{-1}\to N^0$ is an isomorphism. Let $\gamma^i:\det_R(N^i)\otimes_R\det_R(Q^i)\xrightarrow{\sim}\det_R(P^i)$ be the short-exact-sequence map: wedge a basis of the kernel first and lifts of a basis of the quotient second, locally, independently of the chosen lifts. Let $\Gamma_a:D(Q)\otimes_R D(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(P)$ be the map obtained from $\gamma^0$ and the inverse dual of $\gamma^{-1}$, reordering ordinary tensor factors by the symmetry. The determinant $\delta_N=\det(d_N)$ is a trivialization of $D(N)$. Define $T_a:D(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(Q)$ by $\Gamma_a(x\otimes\delta_N)=T_a^{-1}(x)$. These explicitly defined maps have the following calculus: $T_{\mathrm{id}_P}=\mathrm{id}_{D(P)}$; if $a,b:P\to Q$ are degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphisms and $b^0-a^0=d_Qh$, $b^{-1}-a^{-1}=hd_P$ for an $R$-linear $h:P^0\to Q^{-1}$, then $T_a=T_b$; and for degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphisms $a:P\to Q$, $b:Q\to S$, one has $T_{ba}=T_b\circ T_a$.

source.place: Tag 0FJI, construction before Lemma 0FJJ; Tags 0FJK (lemma-homotopic-surjections) and 0FJL (lemma-compose-surjections).

proof.text: The lifting characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] gives sections of each $a^i$; thus $P^i=N^i\oplus Q^i$. If $P^i\oplus E$ is finite free, then $N^i\oplus(Q^i\oplus E)$ is that same finite free module, so $N^i$ is finite projective. Check $d_N$ directly using the cohomology definition in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A kernel element killed by $d_N$ is a cycle of $P^{-1}$ killed by $H^{-1}(a)$, hence zero (there are no degree $-2$ boundaries). For $y\in N^0$, injectivity of $H^0(a)$ implies $y=d_Px$. The element $a^{-1}x$ is a cycle of $Q^{-1}$. Surjectivity of $H^{-1}(a)$ gives a cycle $z\in P^{-1}$ with $a^{-1}z=a^{-1}x$. Then $x-z\in N^{-1}$ and $d_N(x-z)=y$. Thus $d_N$ is bijective.

source.place: Tag 0FJI, construction for surjective quasi-isomorphisms: kernel projectivity and acyclicity.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-projective-determinant-exact-sequence] to the two split exact sequences of Step 1. Its maps are exactly the prescribed $\gamma^i$, with kernel wedges first. Their tensor product, inverse dual in degree $-1$, and ordinary tensor symmetry give $\Gamma_a$. The same node makes the determinant modules invertible; the top exterior map of $d_N$ is an isomorphism of these lines. Under $\operatorname{Hom}(\det N^{-1},\det N^0)=\det N^0\otimes(\det N^{-1})^\vee$, this is a generator $\delta_N$ of $D(N)$. Indeed locally a basis wedge is taken to a basis wedge; its tensor with the dual source wedge is a generator. Inserting this generator in $\Gamma_a$ is an isomorphism $D(Q)\to D(P)$, whose inverse is the stated $T_a$.

source.place: Tag 0FJI, defining triangle for det(a); Tag 0FJB (lemma-det-ses).

proof.text: For $a=\mathrm{id}_P$, its kernel is the zero complex, $D(N)=R$ and $\delta_N=1$. The wedge formula has empty kernel wedge and leaves each quotient wedge unchanged. Hence $\Gamma_a(x\otimes1)=x$ and $T_a=1$.

source.place: Tag 0FJI, zero-kernel case of the definition.

proof.text: For homotopy invariance we may compute at every prime of $R$. The split sequences of Step 1 stay split after localization (apply the same projection and section), and their kernels and differentials are therefore the localized ones. Wedge products, duals of rank-one projectives, and their evaluation maps localize by their basis formulas. Thus $\Gamma_a$, $\delta_N$ and $T_a$ localize to the same construction. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover], all the terms are finite free at each prime: choose a covering element outside that prime and then localize its free basis. Equality there detects equality globally: if an element $y$ in the image of the difference of two maps were nonzero, its proper annihilator would lie in a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$; $y/1=0$ at $\mathfrak m$ would give $sy=0$ for $s\notin\mathfrak m$, a contradiction. For the zero ring all modules are zero and equality is immediate.

Work over one such local ring. Apply [lem-trf-local-common-summand-surjections] to $a^{-1},b^{-1}:P^{-1}\to Q^{-1}$ in chosen finite bases. It gives $U\subseteq P^{-1}$ on which both maps are isomorphisms, including when the target has rank zero. Let $s:Q^{-1}\to U\subseteq P^{-1}$ be the inverse of $a^{-1}|_U$ and put $t=sh:P^0\to P^{-1}$. Then $a^{-1}t=h$.

Put $k^{-1}=1+td_P$ and $k^0=1+d_Pt$. The equations $k^0d_P=d_Pk^{-1}$, $a^{-1}k^{-1}=b^{-1}$, and $a^0k^0=b^0$ follow by expansion and the chain-map equation for $a$. The map $k^{-1}$ is invertible without a finiteness-of-ring assumption: in $P^{-1}=\ker a^{-1}\oplus U$ its matrix is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\ C&B\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, where $B=(a^{-1}|_U)^{-1}(b^{-1}|_U)$ is invertible. Its inverse is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\-B^{-1}C&B^{-1}\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Write $v=(1+td_P)^{-1}$. An inverse for $k^0$ is $1-d_Pvt$: both products equal $1$, using $v+vtd_P=1=v+td_Pv$. Hence $k$ is a chain isomorphism and restricts to an isomorphism $c:N_b\to N_a$ because $ak=b$.

source.place: Tag 0FJK, first two paragraphs; explicit inverse calculation for the chosen lift.

proof.text: In local bases let $A$ be the matrix of $d_P$ and $B$ the matrix of $t$. By [lem-trf-rectangular-determinant-switch], $\det(k^0)=\det(1+AB)=\det(1+BA)=\det(k^{-1})$. Both scalars are units since $k$ is invertible. Consequently the map $D(k)=\det(k^0)\otimes\det(k^{-1})^{-\vee}$ on $D(P)$ is multiplication by their ratio, hence is the identity.

Use the wedge formula of [lem-trf-projective-determinant-exact-sequence] in the diagram with kernel map $c^i$, middle map $k^i$, and quotient map $1$. Applying $k^i$ to a kernel wedge followed by quotient lifts gives the wedge of $c^i$ applied to that kernel basis followed by the images of those lifts, still lifts of the same quotient basis. Thus $\det(k^i)\gamma_b^i=\gamma_a^i(\det(c^i)\otimes1)$. Also $c^0d_{N_b}=d_{N_a}c^{-1}$, so taking exterior powers gives $D(c)\delta_{N_b}=\delta_{N_a}$. Tensor the first equality in the two degrees, inverse-dualizing degree $-1$: $D(k)\Gamma_b(x\otimes\delta_{N_b})=\Gamma_a(x\otimes\delta_{N_a})$. Step 7 makes $D(k)=1$, so $T_b^{-1}=T_a^{-1}$. Step 4 gives $T_b=T_a$ over $R$.

source.place: Tag 0FJK, first paragraph; the wedge naturality of Tag 0FJC (lemma-det-ses-functorial), verified here on generators.

proof.text: For composition put $N=\ker a$, $M=\ker b$, $L=\ker(ba)$. The composite is degreewise surjective and a quasi-isomorphism, since its cohomology maps are compositions of isomorphisms. Thus Step 1 applies to all three kernels. In each degree, $a$ gives an exact sequence $0\to N^i\to L^i\to M^i\to0$: to lift $m\in M^i$ lift it along $a^i$; that lift belongs to $L^i$ since $b^im=0$. These sequences split by [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] since $M^i$ is projective. Let $\eta^i:\det N^i\otimes\det M^i\to\det L^i$ be their wedge maps. Let $\Xi:D(M)\otimes D(N)\to D(L)$ be obtained from $\eta^0$ and its inverse dual in degree $-1$, using ordinary tensor symmetry just as for $\Gamma$.

source.place: Tag 0FJL (lemma-compose-surjections), kernel exact sequences implicit in its hints.

proof.text: The three kernel differentials are isomorphisms and give an isomorphism between the exact sequences of Step 9. Choose bases $n$ of $N^{-1}$ and $m$ of $M^{-1}$ and lifts $\widetilde m$ in $L^{-1}$. Their degree-zero images $d_Nn,d_Mm,d_L\widetilde m$ are corresponding bases and lifts. The wedge of $d_Nn$ followed by $d_L\widetilde m$ is the image by $\det(d_L)$ of the wedge of $n$ followed by $\widetilde m$. Evaluating on these generators gives $\Xi(\delta_M\otimes\delta_N)=\delta_L$. This calculation holds on every simultaneous free localization and hence globally by Step 4's detection argument; the empty wedges give the same formula in rank zero.

source.place: Tag 0FJL, compatibility of the acyclic-kernel trivializations; wedge naturality as in Tag 0FJC.

proof.text:
For each degree use the filtration $N^i\subset L^i\subset P^i$, with successive quotients $M^i,S^i$. Choose local bases $n,m,s$ and choose lifts of $m$ into $L^i$ and of $s$ into $P^i$. Their images in $Q^i$ are lifts of $s$ for $b^i$. Applying first the wedge map for $b^i$ then for $a^i$, or first $\eta^i$ then the map for $(ba)^i$, sends these tensors to the identical ordered wedge $n\wedge\widetilde m\wedge\widetilde s$. Thus these termwise maps agree. Tensoring the degree-zero equality with the inverse dual of the degree-minus-one equality, and using only ordinary tensor symmetry, yields
$$\Gamma_a\bigl(\Gamma_b(x\otimes z_M)\otimes z_N\bigr)=\Gamma_{ba}\bigl(x\otimes\Xi(z_M\otimes z_N)\bigr).$$
Put $z_M=\delta_M$, $z_N=\delta_N$ and use Step 10. The equality becomes $T_a^{-1}T_b^{-1}(x)=T_{ba}^{-1}(x)$, so $T_{ba}=T_bT_a$. The wedge computation also proves compatibility on overlaps, and Step 4 detects the displayed equality globally. All kernel orders are identical in both degrees; there is no graded tensor switch and no extra sign.
